The AI gap between the US and China just hit 3%.

DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash scored 81.1 on LiveBench. Anthropic's top model sits at 83.4. Bloomberg Intelligence confirms this is the narrowest gap they have ever tracked between US and Chinese frontier models.

In May, the gap was 9%. Earlier this year, it was 15%. The compression is accelerating — and it is arriving alongside dramatically lower pricing.

This is no longer an abstract geopolitical headline. It is a real procurement and strategy decision hitting enterprise desks right now.

Chinese open-weight models are offering near-parity performance at a fraction of the cost. But they come with regulatory uncertainty, data sovereignty questions, and supply chain considerations that cannot be waved away.

Meanwhile, Beijing itself is sending mixed signals — new guidelines this week encouraged AI breakthroughs while explicitly warning against speculative investment and poorly coordinated projects.

The bottom line for executives: the cost-performance advantage of US proprietary models is compressing fast. Any AI strategy built around a single vendor or geography is accumulating concentration risk by the quarter.
